back: Release of energy from glucose without oxygen; only glycolysis makes ATP; pyruvate converted to lactate or ethanol to regenerate NAD.
Pyruvate + reduced NAD → lactate + NAD (lactate dehydrogenase).
Pyruvate → ethanal + CO₂; ethanal + reduced NAD → ethanol + NAD.
Glycolysis needs oxidised NAD to accept hydrogen from triose phosphate; without it glycolysis and ATP production stop.
Extra oxygen taken in after exercise to oxidise lactate (in the liver) and restore ATP and oxygen stores.

front: Why is the anaerobic yield small?
back: Only glycolysis makes ATP (net 2); most energy stays in lactate or ethanol.
Aerenchyma; ethanol tolerance (high alcohol dehydrogenase); rapid stem growth to keep leaves above water.
Baking: CO₂ makes dough rise. Brewing: sugars from malted grain fermented to ethanol.
